subject: Week 13: register the baby-lab pools before the 6-month ceiling
bodyText:
This week
This is the first weekly edition — one Saturday email from here on, same structure and sourcing. Week 13 closes the formal newborn period: expect a fully steady head when upright, purposeful reaching with hands meeting at midline, and sustained cooing exchanges, with front-to-back rolling emerging for some (CDC checkpoint: 6 months). The 4-month sleep regression is imminent — the first night fragmenting typically starts within one to three weeks.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Almost-rolling without success — the progression is endogenous and continues regardless of practice volume.
- [monitor] No social smile yet — document and raise at the 4-month visit.
- [monitor] Early sleep fragmenting — likely regression onset rather than illness if feeding and temperament are unchanged.
- [call within 24h] Persistent feeding refusal or a new persistent crying pattern.
- [call now] Fever ≥100.4°F rectal through day 90 — the workup-required threshold still applies (https://www.healthychildren.org/English/health-issues/conditions/fever/Pages/default.aspx); from day 91 a same-day call remains the practical default. Blue lips, labored breathing, or unresponsiveness — 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Register with all four regional baby-lab pools in one sitting this week: Stanford SVNDL is recruiting 3–6-month-olds now with a hard eligibility ceiling at 6 months, plus UC Berkeley BELL, Stanford Language & Cognition, and the UCSF Kids Development Study. Free structured 1:1 sessions with trained researchers — one email session, four registrations, zero dollars. Stanford SVNDL — participate: https://svndl.stanford.edu/participate/
- Enroll Avi in La Petite Baleen's free infant swim tier (ages 2–5 months swim free; 933 Mason St). It buys water acclimation plus grandfathered queue position before paid tuition starts at 6 months ($130–138/mo) — and since there is no dose-response evidence for swim under 12 months, one program is plenty. La Petite Baleen SF: https://www.swimlpb.com/
- Extend tummy time toward 90 min/day cumulative — some infants now tolerate 15–20 min bouts, and chest-off-the-floor push-ups are the current target. AAP: Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Narrate the entire bath, every night — warm water, soap, lift your arm. Conversational turns, not raw word count, predict later language outcomes, and bath runs nightly for the next 18 months, so the cumulative exposure is enormous. Romeo et al. 2018, conversational turns: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 100 (Aug 19, 2026): 100-day mark — book the photo session now if you're marking it.
- Day 112–126 (Aug 31–Sep 14, 2026): 4-month well visit — book this week; vaccines due: RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2.
- Days 98–126 (Aug 17–Sep 14, 2026): typical onset window for the 4-month sleep regression.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete

- Pushes up on elbows during tummy time
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Tripod position. Builds toward eventual rolling.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/pushes-up-on-elbows/complete

- Holds a toy when you put it in his hand
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Voluntary grasp emerging. Soon followed by reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-toy-when-placed/complete

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete
